investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the requested pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence at all — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for peer-pod scheduling. With 0 available VM slots and no preemption victims, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state. The eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (line 1885), which triggers peer-pod provisioning; that provisioning never completes, so the probe times out after ~148–154 seconds and returns a failure message instead of evidence, causing the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256–259 to be violated on all four required fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent or leaked remote-agent VMs are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new probe-created agents.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-peer-pod nodes have affinity rules or labels that exclude remote-agent pods, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 peer-pod nodes and making capacity exhaustion more likely.

Tertiary — VM resource leak from a prior eval run or user session: if a previous remote-agent pod was not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883 may not have run to completion on a prior failure), its kata.peerpods.io/vm slot may still be held, reducing available capacity.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioned for the current load: the 2 peer-pod nodes may have a hard cap on kata.peerpods.io/vm that is too low for concurrent eval runs plus any live user traffic on the same cluster.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, it would indicate a probe-specific bug rather than a shared infrastructure capacity problem.

If a prior eval run's cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs) is confirmed to have completed successfully and no leaked pods are found, the exhaustion would be attributable to live user traffic rather than eval resource leakage.

Consider a canary eval that attempts remote-agent creation with a short timeout (e.g., 30s) and reports a distinct 'capacity-constrained' status when the scheduler returns Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, enabling faster triage than the current 148s timeout.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's required node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent() before it can poll state or exercise the runtime, every downstream check is blocked at pod scheduling, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is ever collected.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. No new remote-agent pod can be scheduled, so the eval runner's createAgent() call times out after ~148 s, the probe exits before writing any evidence, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is entirely unmet. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool, not a code defect in the eval runner itself.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhaustion: the 2 nodes that carry the peerpods VM resource type have no remaining allocatable slots (reported directly by the Kubernetes scheduler in failed-check.message and both sibling messages). This is the primary and most strongly evidenced cause.

Node affinity/selector mismatch for 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling domain is already constrained to those 2 nodes before resource limits are applied. If those 2 nodes are fully occupied, no fallback exists.
Leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or user workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving none available for new probe pods.

Cluster autoscaler not configured or not able to provision additional kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in time: the scheduler message 'No preemption victims found' and 'Preemption is not helpful' indicate no existing pods could be evicted to free capacity.

Eval runner creating a new agent pod per check run without confirming prior cleanup completed, potentially contributing to slot exhaustion across the three concurrent or near-concurrent check runs (remote-agent-create ended at 18:10:33, remote-agent-state ended at 18:13:08, remote-agent-runtime ended at 18:15:38).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the requested pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence at all — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for peer-pod scheduling. With 0 available VM slots and no preemption victims, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state. The eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (line 1885), which triggers peer-pod provisioning; that provisioning never completes, so the probe times out after ~148–154 seconds and returns a failure message instead of evidence, causing the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256–259 to be violated on all four required fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=149856, pod stuck unscheduled for 148s before the check ended.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=154874, evidenceKeys=[].
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduler message (pod stuck 143s), latencyMs=149758, evidenceKeys=[].
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) — the 'remote' machineType triggers peer-pod scheduling.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent or leaked remote-agent VMs are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new probe-created agents.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-peer-pod nodes have affinity rules or labels that exclude remote-agent pods, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 peer-pod nodes and making capacity exhaustion more likely.

Tertiary — VM resource leak from a prior eval run or user session: if a previous remote-agent pod was not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883 may not have run to completion on a prior failure), its kata.peerpods.io/vm slot may still be held, reducing available capacity.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioned for the current load: the 2 peer-pod nodes may have a hard cap on kata.peerpods.io/vm that is too low for concurrent eval runs plus any live user traffic on the same cluster.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's required node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent() before it can poll state or exercise the runtime, every downstream check is blocked at pod scheduling, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is ever collected.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. No new remote-agent pod can be scheduled, so the eval runner's createAgent() call times out after ~148 s, the probe exits before writing any evidence, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is entirely unmet. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool, not a code defect in the eval runner itself.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhaustion: the 2 nodes that carry the peerpods VM resource type have no remaining allocatable slots (reported directly by the Kubernetes scheduler in failed-check.message and both sibling messages). This is the primary and most strongly evidenced cause.

Node affinity/selector mismatch for 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling domain is already constrained to those 2 nodes before resource limits are applied. If those 2 nodes are fully occupied, no fallback exists.
Leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or user workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, leaving none available for new probe pods.

Cluster autoscaler not configured or not able to provision additional kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in time: the scheduler message 'No preemption victims found' and 'Preemption is not helpful' indicate no existing pods could be evicted to free capacity.

Eval runner creating a new agent pod per check run without confirming prior cleanup completed, potentially contributing to slot exhaustion across the three concurrent or near-concurrent check runs (remote-agent-create ended at 18:10:33, remote-agent-state ended at 18:13:08, remote-agent-runtime ended at 18:15:38).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-19 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no agent was created, and the runtime eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production-api cluster. Two nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (0 allocatable units remaining), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on all 6 nodes. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevented agent VM creation entirely, causing all downstream remote-agents eval checks to time out and return no evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 143s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=149758, check timed out well before the 420000ms outage threshold, indicating the pod was stuck from the start rather than slow.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message was ever returned, consistent with the agent pod never starting.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, confirming the probe never reached the runtime response stage.

sibling.remote-agent-state: same Unschedulable message, latencyMs=154874, endedAt=2026-06-19T18:13:08.708Z — the state polling step also failed with the identical scheduler error.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which is the step that triggers pod scheduling; failure here prevents all subsequent evidence collection.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false, confirming the severity classification is eval-infrastructure, not a required-check outage trigger on its own.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots on the two kata-peerpods-capable nodes are consumed by existing pods, leaving zero capacity for new remote agent pods. This directly matches the 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in failed-check.message.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-peerpods nodes carry; the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of resource availability.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning or missing scale-out: the cluster has only 2 nodes capable of hosting kata-peerpods VMs and no autoscaler or node pool expansion triggered to add capacity, leaving no preemption victims and no fallback scheduling path.

Lower confidence — transient burst of concurrent remote agent pod requests saturating the 2 eligible nodes simultaneously during the eval window (all three sibling checks ran within ~5 minutes of each other, each requesting a new pod).

reproductionSteps.details: Identify which workloads are holding the VM slots to determine whether they are stale, leaked, or legitimately active.

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent pod scheduling — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource
affectedAreas.reason: The Kubernetes scheduler explicitly reported 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 eligible nodes, blocking all remote agent pod creation (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes were excluded by node affinity/selector constraints, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 kata-peerpods nodes (failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: remote-agents feature — all three eval checks
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed with the same scheduling error, indicating the entire remote agent provisioning path is blocked (source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189).

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent remote path
affectedAreas.reason: The runner calls createAgent with type 'remote' at line 1918; this is the earliest failure boundary — the pod never schedules, so no subsequent evidence is collected (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918).

recommendedNextActions: Check current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes in the production-api cluster to confirm whether slots are exhausted or leaked.
List all pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resource requests; terminate any stale or leaked pods to free capacity.
Determine whether the cluster's kata-peerpods node pool supports autoscaling or manual scale-out, and trigger expansion if capacity is genuinely exhausted.
Review the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector spec to confirm the 4 non-kata nodes are intentionally excluded and that the constraint is correct.
After restoring capacity, re-run all three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) to confirm recovery.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check to the remote-agent eval runner that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable before attempting pod creation, to produce a clearer SKIP or WARN result instead of a timeout failure.

Note: remote-agent-runtime is marked required=false in infra/evals/status/features.json line 185; however, remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true and also failed, which may trigger the feature's degradedAfterFailures=1 threshold.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval probe to check if failure persists
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the scheduling failure is ongoing or was transient; a pass would produce all 5 required evidence fields and disprove sustained exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Describe the 2 kata-peerpods-capable nodes to inspect vm slot allocatable vs. requested
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms or refutes the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion hypothesis by showing current Allocatable and Requests values on the eligible nodes.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pods with kata.peerpods.io/vm resource requests in the production cluster
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies which workloads are consuming the VM slots, whether any are stale or leaked, and how many slots are in use vs. available.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run remote-agent-create in isolation to confirm the create step is the earliest failure boundary
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Isolates whether the scheduling failure occurs at pod creation time (remote-agent-create) independently of the runtime and state checks.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect implicated eval source paths for any recent changes to remote agent pod spec or node selector configuration
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether a recent change to the pod spec, node affinity, or resource request contributed to the scheduling failure.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 kata-peerpods nodes shows available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude the kata-peerpods nodes entirely, the 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message would be a red herring and the affinity mismatch would be the sole cause.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds and produces all 5 required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent pod requests) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If sibling checks for local agents (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) also failed at the same time with unrelated errors, a broader cluster or API-plane issue may be the real cause rather than kata-peerpods-specific capacity.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is registered on any node in the cluster, the resource was never provisioned and the issue is a missing node pool rather than exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on all eligible nodes and warns when available slots fall below a minimum threshold, catching exhaustion before pod scheduling attempts fail.

Add a pre-scheduling readiness check within the remote-agent eval runner that verifies at least one schedulable node with available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity exists before calling createAgent, surfacing a WARN instead of a timeout.
Add a concurrent-scheduling stress eval that attempts to create multiple remote agent pods simultaneously to characterize the cluster's burst capacity and detect slot exhaustion under load.

Add a node-affinity validation eval that confirms the expected number of nodes match the remote agent pod's affinity/selector constraints, alerting if the eligible node count drops below the expected minimum.
